text: Listen closely, boys... there's no time before it surfaces again.
Drop the jokes.
I know that man.
I stood beneath the towering arches of Caer Callidyr... before he cast me into the dark!
Look through my memory!
Rain lashes the stained glass of Tyr's sanctum.
Your mother has vanished into the dark... leaving no trace behind...
and upon the cold stone lie two small boys... you!
Pale as chalk, drowning in sweat, with a black, unnatural poison creeping through your veins toward your hearts!
No healer in the realm could break it.
And there, stripped of his armor and pride, kneels a younger Valerys...
terrified of losing the only pieces of her he has left!
Their mother is gone, Tyr... do not take them from me too!
Take me instead!
Strip my title, take my honor, take every breath left in my lungs!
Just burn this poison from my boys... let them live!
The torches freeze into blinding white fire without heat.
Shadows stretch like iron bars across the stone.
And the one-handed god answers...
not like thunder, no, like a thousand blades drawn at once:
The Law demands balance, Valerys. No life is given without a price.
These boys carry blood that the darkness already hunts.
If I am to pull them from the grave, you must become the wall that keeps the shadow out.
Name the price. Anything!
Your sword and your oath belong to Caer Callidyr.
You will never cross this city's gates again—
neither to hunt their mother, nor to ride to their aid.
You will be the city's shield for as long as your heart beats.
The day you place your own blood above your post and step beyond these walls, the contract is shattered—
and the very oath you swore will consume you.
See the agony in his eyes!
In that single heartbeat, he realizes the terrible choice:
to keep you breathing, he must abandon the search for your mother forever!
He knows he must send little Cedric away to the monastery to hide your blood from the cult...
and he must hold Arthas at arm's length, cold and distant,
terrified that if he ever lets himself love you openly, he will grow weak enough to break his vow and doom you all!
Still, he doesn't flinch.
He lays his sword at the foot of the altar
and opens his arms to Tyr's blinding judgment—letting the god's searing golden light wash over you,
burning the poison from your veins while forging his own soul to the city's stone!
Then let it be the law.
Let my life be their chain.
Tyr never betrayed him!
Your father bought your lives with his own—and he shattered that chain in Duncastle just to save you!
Stop praying to a god who has already collected his due!
His only chance of survival is to deny his oath to Tyr... before that beast tears through the stone again!
